# ~/.zshrc: interactive zsh configuration.
#
# Load order. Each phase depends only on the phases above it:
#   1. Instant prompt    Powerlevel10k draws a cached prompt at once. Keep first.
#   2. Helpers           path/fpath dedup and the output cache used below.
#   3. Environment       Plain exports and the (cached) Homebrew environment.
#   4. PATH              One ordered list, highest precedence first.
#   5. Zinit             Plugin manager, theme, and fzf: what the first prompt needs.
#   6. Completion files  fpath entries and generated completion scripts.
#   7. Turbo             Loads just after the first prompt: compinit, the
#                        completion extras, git helpers, syntax highlighting.
#   8. Functions
#   9. mise              Must stay last. See the note there.
#
# Shells without job control (`zsh -ic` from agent harnesses) skip everything
# that needs ZLE: the instant prompt, the theme and the fzf key bindings. Turbo
# plugins never load in `zsh -c` shells, because no prompt is ever drawn.

### 1. Powerlevel10k instant prompt ###########################################
# Initialization code that may require console input (password prompts, [y/n]
# confirmations, etc.) must go above this block; everything else may go below.
# Skipped without job control: instant prompt needs `setopt monitor`, which
# fails there and takes gitstatus down with it.
if [[ -o monitor && -r "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/p10k-instant-prompt-${(%):-%n}.zsh" ]]; then
  source "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/p10k-instant-prompt-${(%):-%n}.zsh"
fi

### 2. Helpers ################################################################
# Keep only the first occurrence of each entry. Prepending an entry that is
# already present therefore moves it to the front instead of duplicating it,
# and nested shells no longer grow PATH/fpath.
typeset -gU path fpath

typeset -g ZSHRC_CACHE="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/zsh"

# .zshrc-cache <file> <source> <command...>
# Writes the output of <command> to <file> unless <file> is newer than
# <source>, the binary or script that produces it. It also regenerates when
# <source> resolves to a different path: this catches upgrades of symlinked
# binaries whose targets keep a fixed mtime (Nix store paths have mtime 1).
# Returns non-zero when <source> is missing or <command> fails.
.zshrc-cache() {
  local file=$1 src=$2 stamp="${1:h}/.${1:t}.source"
  shift 2
  [[ -n $src && -e $src ]] || return 1
  src=${src:A}
  [[ -s $file && $file -nt $src && -r $stamp && "$(<$stamp)" == "$src" ]] && return 0
  command mkdir -p -- "${file:h}" || return 1
  if "$@" >| "$file.$$" 2>/dev/null && [[ -s "$file.$$" ]]; then
    command mv -f -- "$file.$$" "$file" && print -r -- "$src" >| "$stamp"
  else
    command rm -f -- "$file.$$"
    return 1
  fi
}

# .zshrc-source-cached <name> <source> <command...>
# Replaces `eval "$(command)"` for init scripts whose output only changes
# when <source> changes.
.zshrc-source-cached() {
  local file="$ZSHRC_CACHE/init/$1.zsh"
  shift
  .zshrc-cache "$file" "$@" && source "$file"
}

### 3. Environment ############################################################
export LANG=en_US.UTF-8

export MATLAB_RUNTIME="/Applications/MATLAB/MATLAB_Runtime/v97"
export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH="${MATLAB_RUNTIME}/runtime/maci64:${MATLAB_RUNTIME}/sys/os/maci64:${MATLAB_RUNTIME}/bin/maci64"

export PNPM_HOME="${HOME}/Library/pnpm"

### Alibaba cloud mirror for homebrew
# export HOMEBREW_API_DOMAIN=https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew-bottles/api
# export HOMEBREW_BOTTLE_DOMAIN=https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew-bottles
# export HOMEBREW_BREW_GIT_REMOTE=https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew/brew.git

# Homebrew sets HOMEBREW_*, MANPATH and INFOPATH, and puts its site-functions
# on fpath before compinit. `brew shellenv` costs ~25 ms, so its output is
# cached and regenerated only when brew's shellenv.sh changes. It runs with a
# minimal PATH because brew prints nothing when its dirs already lead PATH
# (nested shells), which would poison the cache.
.zshrc-source-cached brew-shellenv /opt/homebrew/Library/Homebrew/cmd/shellenv.sh \
  env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin /opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv zsh

### 4. PATH ###################################################################
# The single place that decides command precedence, highest first. Because
# path is unique (phase 2), each directory lands exactly where it is listed,
# whatever /etc/zprofile's path_helper, ~/.zprofile, brew's path_helper call
# or a parent shell already put in PATH. When an installer appends a PATH line
# to this file, move the directory into this list instead.
#
# Two layers still go on top at runtime: zinit-managed programs (phase 5)
# and mise tools (phase 9).
path=(
  "${HOME}/.bend/bin"
  "${HOME}/.kimi-code/bin"
  "${HOME}/.opencode/bin"
  "${HOME}/.local/bin"                     # uv, mise, Antigravity CLI
  "${PNPM_HOME}/bin"
  "${HOME}/.deno/bin"
  "${HOME}/.nix-profile/bin"               # Nix beats Homebrew on overlap (git, ffmpeg)
  /nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin
  "${HOMEBREW_PREFIX:-/opt/homebrew}/bin"
  "${HOMEBREW_PREFIX:-/opt/homebrew}/sbin"
  # Below Homebrew: tools with unique names that never need to override it.
  "${HOME}/Develop/google-cloud-sdk/bin"
  "${HOME}/go/bin"
  "${HOME}/.grok/bin"
  "${HOME}/.bun/bin"
  "${HOME}/.mint/bin"
  $path                                    # login PATH: /etc/paths, zshenv, ~/.zprofile
  "${HOME}/.cache/lm-studio/bin"           # LM Studio CLI (lms), lowest
)

### 5. Zinit and synchronous plugins ##########################################
ZINIT_HOME="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/zinit/zinit.git"
if [[ ! -f "$ZINIT_HOME/zinit.zsh" ]]; then
  print -P "%F{33} %F{220}Installing %F{33}ZDHARMA-CONTINUUM%F{220} Initiative Plugin Manager (%F{33}zdharma-continuum/zinit%F{220})…%f"
  command mkdir -p "${ZINIT_HOME:h}" && command chmod g-rwX "${ZINIT_HOME:h}"
  command git clone https://github.com/zdharma-continuum/zinit "$ZINIT_HOME" && \
    print -P "%F{33} %F{34}Installation successful.%f%b" || \
    print -P "%F{160} The clone has failed.%f%b"
fi
source "$ZINIT_HOME/zinit.zsh"

# Terminal and prompt. Both are skipped where they do nothing: iTerm2's
# integration outside iTerm2, and the theme without job control (no prompt
# to render, and gitstatus/ZLE initialization would fail noisily).
if [[ $TERM_PROGRAM == iTerm.app || $LC_TERMINAL == iTerm2 ]] && [[ -r "${HOME}/.iterm2_shell_integration.zsh" ]]; then
  source "${HOME}/.iterm2_shell_integration.zsh"
fi
if [[ -o monitor ]]; then
  zinit depth"1" light-mode for romkatv/powerlevel10k
  # To customize prompt, run `p10k configure` or edit ~/.p10k.zsh.
  [[ -r ~/.p10k.zsh ]] && source ~/.p10k.zsh
fi

# fzf binary from GitHub releases. Its shell integration (Ctrl-T/Ctrl-R/Alt-C
# and `**<Tab>`) is written to init.zsh once per install or update, so startup
# runs no `fzf --zsh` subprocess. The key bindings need ZLE, so init.zsh is
# not sourced without job control.
zinit ice from"gh-r" as"program" atclone"./fzf --zsh >| init.zsh" atpull"%atclone"
[[ -o monitor ]] && zinit ice src"init.zsh"
zinit light junegunn/fzf

### 6. Completion files #######################################################
# compinit (phase 7) indexes every _file on fpath. The completion function
# loads on first use, which is cheaper than an eval of the script at startup.
fpath=(
  "$ZSHRC_CACHE/completions"               # generated below
  "${HOME}/.zsh/completions"               # deno
  "${HOME}/.grok/completions/zsh"          # after an upgrade: grok completions zsh > ~/.grok/completions/zsh/_grok
  $fpath                                   # incl. Homebrew site-functions and zinit's completions
)

# CLIs that print their completion script. Cached as fpath files and
# regenerated when the binary changes.
.zshrc-cache "$ZSHRC_CACHE/completions/_uv" "${commands[uv]}" uv generate-shell-completion zsh
.zshrc-cache "$ZSHRC_CACHE/completions/_uvx" "${commands[uvx]}" uvx --generate-shell-completion zsh

### 7. Turbo: loaded right after the first prompt ##############################
# .zshrc-compdump-is-fresh <dump>
# Returns 0 when the completion dump can be trusted as-is, so compinit runs
# with -C: no compaudit and no rescan of fpath. Returns 1 to make compinit
# audit fpath and rebuild the dump if the set of completion files changed.
.zshrc-compdump-is-fresh() {
  local dump=$1
  # TODO(you): choose the invalidation policy. Returning 1 always keeps the
  # full check on every shell, which is the previous behavior.
  return 1
}

.zshrc-compinit() {
  local dump="${ZINIT[ZCOMPDUMP_PATH]:-${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zcompdump}"
  if .zshrc-compdump-is-fresh "$dump"; then
    ZINIT[COMPINIT_OPTS]=-C
  else
    ZINIT[COMPINIT_OPTS]=
  fi
  zicompinit
  # compinit sources the dump; zsh reads dump.zwc instead when it is newer.
  [[ -s $dump && ! "$dump.zwc" -nt $dump ]] && zcompile -- "$dump"
}

# Completions registered by code instead of fpath files. They need compdef,
# so they run after compinit (atload runs after zinit restores compdef).
.zshrc-completion-extras() {
  # gcloud, gsutil and bq ship bash completions (loads bashcompinit).
  local gcloud_completion="${HOME}/Develop/google-cloud-sdk/completion.zsh.inc"
  [[ -r $gcloud_completion ]] && source "$gcloud_completion"
  compdef _gnu_generic zed
}

# Listed order is load order. compinit runs in the atinit of the last plugin,
# after the plugins above it have loaded: compdef calls those plugins make
# earlier are captured and replayed by zicdreplay. fast-syntax-highlighting
# loads last because it wraps every ZLE widget that exists when it loads.
# blockf: git-ignore's completion is already linked into zinit's completions
# dir, so its fpath entry is not needed.
zinit wait lucid light-mode for \
    alexiszamanidis/zsh-git-fzf \
  blockf \
    laggardkernel/git-ignore \
  atinit".zshrc-compinit; zicdreplay" atload".zshrc-completion-extras" \
    zdharma-continuum/fast-syntax-highlighting

### 8. Functions ##############################################################
# gitignore.io templates. Takes several names: `gi macos node`.
function gi() { curl -sLw "\n" "https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore/api/${(j:,:)@}" }

### 9. mise: must stay last ###################################################
# Its precmd hook rebuilds PATH from the snapshot taken at activation, which
# demotes every prepend after this line (e.g. nix bash below /bin/bash).
# Invoked by absolute path so it doesn't rely on PATH.
eval "$(~/.local/bin/mise activate zsh)"

# Add deno completions to search path
if [[ ":$FPATH:" != *":/Users/jessearmand/.zsh/completions:"* ]]; then export FPATH="/Users/jessearmand/.zsh/completions:$FPATH"; fi
# Enable Powerlevel10k instant prompt. Should stay close to the top of ~/.zshrc.
# Initialization code that may require console input (password prompts, [y/n]
# confirmations, etc.) must go above this block; everything else may go below.
# Skip when job control is unavailable (interactive zsh without a tty, e.g.
# `zsh -ic` from agent harnesses): instant prompt needs `setopt monitor`,
# which fails there and takes gitstatus down with it.
if [[ -o monitor && -r "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/p10k-instant-prompt-${(%):-%n}.zsh" ]]; then
  source "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/p10k-instant-prompt-${(%):-%n}.zsh"
fi

export LANG=en_US.UTF-8

export PATH="${HOME}/.local/bin:$PATH"

test -e "${HOME}/.iterm2_shell_integration.zsh" && source "${HOME}/.iterm2_shell_integration.zsh"

export MATLAB_RUNTIME="/Applications/MATLAB/MATLAB_Runtime/v97"
export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH="${MATLAB_RUNTIME}/runtime/maci64:${MATLAB_RUNTIME}/sys/os/maci64:${MATLAB_RUNTIME}/bin/maci64"

# Added by LM Studio CLI tool (lms)
export PATH="$PATH:${HOME}/.cache/lm-studio/bin"
export PATH="${HOME}/.mint/bin:$PATH"
export PATH="${HOME}/.bun/bin:$PATH"
export PATH="$HOME/.grok/bin:$PATH"

export PATH="${HOME}/Develop/google-cloud-sdk/bin:$PATH"

export PATH="${HOME}/go/bin:$PATH"

### Alibaba cloud mirror for homebrew
# export HOMEBREW_API_DOMAIN=https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew-bottles/api
# export HOMEBREW_BOTTLE_DOMAIN=https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew-bottles
# export HOMEBREW_BREW_GIT_REMOTE=https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew/brew.git

### Added by Zinit's installer
if [[ ! -f $HOME/.local/share/zinit/zinit.git/zinit.zsh ]]; then
    print -P "%F{33} %F{220}Installing %F{33}ZDHARMA-CONTINUUM%F{220} Initiative Plugin Manager (%F{33}zdharma-continuum/zinit%F{220})…%f"
    command mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/share/zinit" && command chmod g-rwX "$HOME/.local/share/zinit"
    command git clone https://github.com/zdharma-continuum/zinit "$HOME/.local/share/zinit/zinit.git" && \
        print -P "%F{33} %F{34}Installation successful.%f%b" || \
        print -P "%F{160} The clone has failed.%f%b"
fi

source "$HOME/.local/share/zinit/zinit.git/zinit.zsh"
autoload -Uz _zinit
(( ${+_comps} )) && _comps[zinit]=_zinit

# Load a few important annexes, without Turbo
# (this is currently required for annexes)
zinit light-mode for \
    zdharma-continuum/zinit-annex-as-monitor \
    zdharma-continuum/zinit-annex-bin-gem-node \
    zdharma-continuum/zinit-annex-patch-dl \
    zdharma-continuum/zinit-annex-rust

### End of Zinit's installer chunk
#
# Load powerlevel10k theme (skipped without job control — no prompt to render,
# and gitstatus/zle initialization would fail noisily).
if [[ -o monitor ]]; then
  zinit ice depth"1" # git clone depth
  zinit light romkatv/powerlevel10k
fi

# Binary release in archive, from GitHub-releases page.
# After automatic unpacking it provides program "fzf".
zi ice from"gh-r" as"program"
zi light junegunn/fzf

# Load completion-related plugins with wait"0"
zinit lucid wait"0" for \
  lincheney/fzf-tab-completion \
  alexiszamanidis/zsh-git-fzf \
  laggardkernel/git-ignore

# Grok CLI tab completions (regenerate after upgrade:
#   grok completions zsh > ~/.grok/completions/zsh/_grok)
[[ -d "$HOME/.grok/completions/zsh" ]] && fpath=("$HOME/.grok/completions/zsh" $fpath)

zicompinit
zinit cdreplay -q

zinit light zdharma-continuum/fast-syntax-highlighting

# Set up fzf key bindings (Ctrl-T/Ctrl-R/Alt-C) and fuzzy completion.
# Skipped without job control: bindings are useless without ZLE, and fzf's
# option save/restore eval fails noisily on the unsettable `zle` option.
command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -o monitor ]] && source <(fzf --zsh)

# The next line updates PATH for the Google Cloud SDK.
if [ -f "${HOME}/Develop/google-cloud-sdk/path.zsh.inc" ]; then . "${HOME}/Develop/google-cloud-sdk/path.zsh.inc"; fi

# The next line enables shell command completion for gcloud.
if [ -f "${HOME}/Develop/google-cloud-sdk/completion.zsh.inc" ]; then . "${HOME}/Develop/google-cloud-sdk/completion.zsh.inc"; fi

function gi() { curl -sLw "\n" https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore/api/$@ ;}

eval "$(uv generate-shell-completion zsh)"
eval "$(uvx --generate-shell-completion zsh)"

eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"

### PATH precedence — everything below MUST stay after `brew shellenv`.
# path_helper (run by `brew shellenv`) rebuilds PATH with /etc/paths +
# /etc/paths.d (including /opt/homebrew/bin) up front, demoting every prepend
# earlier in this file. Entries that must outrank homebrew are (re-)prepended
# here; later prepends win. Final precedence:
#   ~/.local/bin > pnpm > deno > nix profile > homebrew > system
# See README "PATH ordering in zshrc" for the full reasoning.

# Nix profile beats homebrew on overlap (e.g. git, ffmpeg).
export PATH="$HOME/.nix-profile/bin:/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin:$PATH"

# deno (the env file guards against duplicate prepends)
. "$HOME/.deno/env"

# pnpm
export PNPM_HOME="${HOME}/Library/pnpm"
case ":$PATH:" in
  *":$PNPM_HOME/bin:"*) ;;
  *) export PATH="$PNPM_HOME/bin:$PATH" ;;
esac
# pnpm end

# Re-prepend ~/.local/bin (Antigravity CLI installer). The early prepend near
# the top of this file stays load-bearing — mise activate and the uv/uvx
# completion evals need it during startup — this one restores its precedence.
export PATH="${HOME}/.local/bin:$PATH"

compdef _gnu_generic zed

# bun completions
[ -s "/opt/homebrew/share/zsh/site-functions/_bun" ] && source "/opt/homebrew/share/zsh/site-functions/_bun"

# To customize prompt, run `p10k configure` or edit ~/.p10k.zsh.
[[ ! -o monitor || ! -f ~/.p10k.zsh ]] || source ~/.p10k.zsh

# opencode
export PATH="${HOME}/.opencode/bin:$PATH"

# kimi-code
export PATH="${HOME}/.kimi-code/bin:$PATH"

# bend
export PATH="${HOME}/.bend/bin:$PATH"

# mise must come last: its precmd hook rebuilds PATH from the snapshot taken
# at activation, demoting every prepend after this line (e.g. nix bash below
# /bin/bash). Invoked by absolute path so it doesn't rely on PATH.
eval "$(~/.local/bin/mise activate zsh)"

input.old_string:
# fzf binary from GitHub releases. Its shell integration (Ctrl-T/Ctrl-R/Alt-C
# and `**<Tab>`) is written to init.zsh once per install or update, so startup
# runs no `fzf --zsh` subprocess. The key bindings need ZLE, so init.zsh is
# not sourced without job control.
zinit ice from"gh-r" as"program" atclone"./fzf --zsh >| init.zsh" atpull"%atclone"
[[ -o monitor ]] && zinit ice src"init.zsh"
zinit light junegunn/fzf
input.new_string:

[[ -o monitor ]] && .zshrc-source-cached fzf "${commands[fzf]}" fzf --zsh

fpath=(
  "$ZSHRC_CACHE/completions"               # generated below
  "${HOME}/.zsh/completions"               # deno
  "${HOME}/.grok/completions/zsh"          # after an upgrade: grok completions zsh > ~/.grok/completions/zsh/_grok
  $fpath                                   # incl. Homebrew site-functions and zinit's completions
)

# CLIs that print their completion script. Cached as fpath files and
# regenerated when the binary changes.
.zshrc-cache "$ZSHRC_CACHE/completions/_uv" "${commands[uv]}" uv generate-shell-completion zsh
.zshrc-cache "$ZSHRC_CACHE/completions/_uvx" "${commands[uvx]}" uvx --generate-shell-completion zsh

### 7. Turbo: loaded right after the first prompt ##############################
# .zshrc-compdump-is-fresh <dump>
# Returns 0 when the completion dump can be trusted as-is, so compinit runs
# with -C: no compaudit and no rescan of fpath. Returns 1 to make compinit
# audit fpath and rebuild the dump if the set of completion files changed.
.zshrc-compdump-is-fresh() {
  local dump=$1
  # TODO(you): choose the invalidation policy. Returning 1 always keeps the
  # full check on every shell, which is the previous behavior.
  return 1
}

.zshrc-compinit() {
  local dump="${ZINIT[ZCOMPDUMP_PATH]:-${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zcompdump}"
  if .zshrc-compdump-is-fresh "$dump"; then
    ZINIT[COMPINIT_OPTS]=-C
  else
    ZINIT[COMPINIT_OPTS]=
  fi
  zicompinit
  # compinit sources the dump; zsh reads dump.zwc instead when it is newer.
  [[ -s $dump && ! "$dump.zwc" -nt $dump ]] && zcompile -- "$dump"
}

# Completions registered by code instead of fpath files. They need compdef,
# so they run after compinit (atload runs after zinit restores compdef).
.zshrc-completion-extras() {
  # gcloud, gsutil and bq ship bash completions (loads bashcompinit).
  local gcloud_completion="${HOME}/Develop/google-cloud-sdk/completion.zsh.inc"
  [[ -r $gcloud_completion ]] && source "$gcloud_completion"
  compdef _gnu_generic zed
}

# Listed order is load order. compinit runs in the atinit of the last plugin,
# after the plugins above it have loaded: compdef calls those plugins make
# earlier are captured and replayed by zicdreplay. fast-syntax-highlighting
# loads last because it wraps every ZLE widget that exists when it loads.
# blockf: git-ignore's completion is already linked into zinit's completions
# dir, so its fpath entry is not needed.
zinit wait lucid light-mode for \
    alexiszamanidis/zsh-git-fzf \
  blockf \
    laggardkernel/git-ignore \
  atinit".zshrc-compinit; zicdreplay" atload".zshrc-completion-extras" \
    zdharma-continuum/fast-syntax-highlighting

### 8. Functions ##############################################################
# gitignore.io templates. Takes several names: `gi macos node`.
function gi() { curl -sLw "\n" "https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore/api/${(j:,:)@}" }

### 9. mise: must stay last ###################################################
# Its precmd hook rebuilds PATH from the snapshot taken at activation, which
# demotes every prepend after this line (e.g. nix bash below /bin/bash).
# Invoked by absolute path so it doesn't rely on PATH.
eval "$(~/.local/bin/mise activate zsh)"

  return 1

PATH ordering in zshrc
----------------------

`zshrc` has two PATH zones, split by `eval "$(brew shellenv)"`:

- `brew shellenv` runs macOS `path_helper`, which **rebuilds** PATH: it
  front-loads `/etc/paths` + `/etc/paths.d/*` (including
  `/opt/homebrew/bin`), then re-appends previously-set entries behind them.
  Every prepend *before* that line (mint, bun, grok, go, gcloud, cargo)
  therefore ends up **below** homebrew — harmless for uniquely-named
  binaries, but useless for overriding anything.
- Entries that must outrank homebrew live in the marked block *after*
  `brew shellenv`, where later prepends win. Final precedence:

      mise tools > ~/.local/bin > pnpm > deno > nix profile > homebrew > system

`~/.local/bin` appears twice on purpose: the early prepend is load-bearing
(the `uv`/`uvx` completion evals need those binaries during startup); the
late one restores its precedence after `path_helper` demotes it.

`mise activate` is the **last** line. Its precmd hook rebuilds PATH from the
snapshot taken at activation, so anything prepended after it gets demoted
behind `/bin` before the first prompt — with it near the top, `bash`
resolved to macOS's 3.2 instead of nix's `bashInteractive` despite the nix
prepend. Keep every PATH export above it.

When an installer appends a PATH line to `~/.zshrc`, move it into the
marked block — its position decides whether it can override brew/nix at all.

ZINIT_HOME="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/zinit/zinit.git"
if [[ ! -f "$ZINIT_HOME/zinit.zsh" ]]; then
  print -P "%F{33} %F{220}Installing %F{33}ZDHARMA-CONTINUUM%F{220} Initiative Plugin Manager (%F{33}zdharma-continuum/zinit%F{220})…%f"
  command mkdir -p "${ZINIT_HOME:h}" && command chmod g-rwX "${ZINIT_HOME:h}"
  command git clone https://github.com/zdharma-continuum/zinit "$ZINIT_HOME" && \
    print -P "%F{33} %F{34}Installation successful.%f%b" || \
    print -P "%F{160} The clone has failed.%f%b"
fi
source "$ZINIT_HOME/zinit.zsh"

# Terminal and prompt. Both are skipped where they do nothing: iTerm2's
# integration outside iTerm2, and the theme without job control (no prompt
# to render, and gitstatus/ZLE initialization would fail noisily).
if [[ $TERM_PROGRAM == iTerm.app || $LC_TERMINAL == iTerm2 ]] && [[ -r "${HOME}/.iterm2_shell_integration.zsh" ]]; then
  source "${HOME}/.iterm2_shell_integration.zsh"
fi
if [[ -o monitor ]]; then
  zinit depth"1" light-mode for romkatv/powerlevel10k
  # To customize prompt, run `p10k configure` or edit ~/.p10k.zsh.
  [[ -r ~/.p10k.zsh ]] && source ~/.p10k.zsh
fi

# fzf binary from GitHub releases. Its shell integration (Ctrl-T/Ctrl-R/Alt-C
# and `**<Tab>`) is cached and regenerated when `zinit update` replaces the
# binary. Not sourced without job control: the bindings need ZLE, and fzf's
# option save/restore fails noisily on the unsettable `zle` option.
zinit from"gh-r" as"program" light-mode for junegunn/fzf
[[ -o monitor ]] && .zshrc-source-cached fzf "${commands[fzf]}" fzf --zsh

onto one current revision with `nix profile upgrade --all`. To pin to a stable
release instead, repoint the registry: `nix registry add nixpkgs github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-26.05`.

## The PATH ordering trap (critical on macOS)

`brew shellenv` invokes `/usr/libexec/path_helper -s`, which **rebuilds** PATH
from `/etc/paths` plus `/etc/paths.d/*` first, then appends your existing PATH.
Brew's installer drops `/etc/paths.d/homebrew`, so this front-loads
`/opt/homebrew/bin` on every shell startup, defeating any earlier `export
PATH="$HOME/.nix-profile/bin:$PATH"`.

Fix: re-prepend nix paths *after* `brew shellenv`. In `~/.zshrc`:

```sh
eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"

# `brew shellenv` runs path_helper which front-loads /opt/homebrew/bin.
# Re-prepend nix paths so nix profile beats homebrew on overlap (e.g. git, ffmpeg).
export PATH="$HOME/.nix-profile/bin:/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin:$PATH"
```

Without this, you'll install nix versions of tools and silently keep using
brew's because of PATH precedence. The Determinate Nix installer adds nix to
PATH via `/etc/zshrc` (which runs *before* `~/.zshrc`), and `brew shellenv`
later overrides that.

Two extra failure modes surface when the fix *looks* present but isn't effective:

- **Stale / unsymlinked dotfiles.** If `~/.zshrc` is a hand-managed copy that has
  drifted from your tracked repo (this repo is not symlinked — see `CLAUDE.md`),
  the fix can be committed to the repo yet absent from the *running* file. Symptom
  is identical (brew wins). Verify the LIVE file, not the repo:
  `rg nix-profile ~/.zshrc`, then confirm with `zsh -lic 'command -v git'`.
- **Hardcoded `/opt/homebrew` paths in configs.** `gh auth setup-git` writes
  `helper = !/opt/homebrew/bin/gh auth git-credential` into `~/.gitconfig` with an
  *absolute* brew path. Uninstalling brew `gh` then breaks GitHub HTTPS auth
  silently. Rewrite to PATH-relative `!gh auth git-credential`. Before any brew
  uninstall, audit: `rg -l /opt/homebrew ~/.gitconfig ~/.zshrc ~/.config 2>/dev/null`.

content.content:
## The PATH ordering trap (critical on macOS)

`brew shellenv` invokes `/usr/libexec/path_helper -s`, which **rebuilds** PATH
from `/etc/paths` plus `/etc/paths.d/*` first, then appends your existing PATH.
Brew's installer drops `/etc/paths.d/homebrew`, so this front-loads
`/opt/homebrew/bin` on every shell startup, defeating any earlier `export
PATH="$HOME/.nix-profile/bin:$PATH"`.

Fix: make PATH order independent of what ran before it. `zshrc` declares
`typeset -U path`, runs `brew shellenv`, and only then assigns one ordered
list (phase 4 of `zshrc`). With `-U`, the assignment moves every listed
directory to its listed position:

```sh
typeset -gU path
path=(
  ...
  "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin"          # nix beats homebrew on overlap (git, ffmpeg)
  /nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin
  /opt/homebrew/bin /opt/homebrew/sbin
  ...
  $path                             # whatever path_helper and the login shell set
)
```

Without this, you'll install nix versions of tools and silently keep using
brew's because of PATH precedence. The Determinate Nix installer adds nix to
PATH via `/etc/zshrc` (which runs *before* `~/.zshrc`), and `brew shellenv`
later overrides that.

content.text:
I rewrote `zshrc` into nine numbered phases. The shell now reaches its first prompt in about half the time, and completions, key bindings and PATH lookups behave the same as before. I haven't committed anything. Your uncommitted edits (the fast-syntax-highlighting switch, the `$HOME` paths, bend) are all kept.

**Timings** (fresh login shell under a pty, median of repeated runs):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| End of `zshrc` (no more lag on keys you type early) | ~212 ms | ~97 ms |
| First real prompt | ~241 ms | ~118 ms |
| Everything loaded, including Turbo | ~320 ms | ~198 ms |

To check nothing broke, I captured the shell state from the old and new files in clean environments and diffed them. Key bindings, options, which binary each command resolves to, and exported variables are identical. The completion mappings are identical too, apart from a few new ones listed below. Nested shells, `zsh -ic` shells and cache refreshes also work.

**Where the time went, and the fixes**
- **uv/uvx completions (~58 ms):** these ran through `eval` on every start. Their output is now cached as `_uv` and `_uvx` files that zsh loads on first use.
- **`brew shellenv` (~27 ms) and `fzf --zsh` (~5 ms):** both are cached. A small helper, `.zshrc-cache`, regenerates a cached file when the program that makes it changes, or when it now points at a different install (which covers Nix upgrades). The brew cache is built with a clean PATH, because brew prints nothing when its directories already lead PATH.
- **Syntax highlighting (~25 ms):** fast-syntax-highlighting is back in Turbo (loaded just after the first prompt) and loads last. It now also covers fzf's widgets.
- **zinit extras (~4 ms):** I removed the four annexes. None of the options they add were used anywhere in the file.

**Easier to follow**
- **PATH is one list:** the list in phase 4 goes from highest to lowest precedence, and `typeset -U path` puts each directory exactly where it is listed. Before, precedence depended on where each line sat relative to brew's reordering. Nested shells also didn't match fresh ones: pnpm and deno lost their priority, and `~/.local/bin` appeared twice.
- **Why compinit is not in Turbo:** zinit's docs suggest deferring compinit. But your mise version (2026.9.15) runs its own `compinit -i` if completions aren't set up yet, and registers tool completions such as `_fnox`. Deferring would run compinit twice and wipe those. I hit this during testing, so compinit stays synchronous and a comment explains why.

**Problems found along the way**
- `lincheney/fzf-tab-completion` never did anything: the repo has no file zinit knows to load, so it loaded nothing. I removed it. If you want Tab to open fzf, add `pick"zsh/fzf-zsh-completion.sh" atload"bindkey '^I' fzf_completion"` to it in the Turbo block. Be aware that this replaces fzf's `**<Tab>` binding.
- iTerm2 shell integration was loading in Ghostty and printing iTerm2 escape codes into `zsh -ic` output. It now only loads inside iTerm2.
- Homebrew's completion folder was added to fpath after compinit, so its completions were missed. That's why you had to `source` `_bun` by hand. It's now on fpath first, which adds `_brew`, `_mole` and `_wezterm`.
- `gi macos node` sent curl two separate URLs. It now joins the names with commas, which is what the API expects.

I also updated `README.md` and `nix-migration.md` to describe the new PATH and compinit ordering. A copy of your previous `zshrc` is in the session scratchpad at `zshrc.before-refactor`.

**Worth running yourself**
- `zinit self-update`: your zinit is 147 commits behind upstream.
- `zinit delete zsh-users/zsh-syntax-highlighting lincheney/fzf-tab-completion` and the four annexes, to remove their leftover folders.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `typeset -U path` keeps the *first* copy of each entry. So a single `path=(… $path …)` assignment reorders PATH as a whole, instead of relying on a chain of later prepends to win.
- A Nix store file's mtime is always 1970, so "is the cache newer than the binary?" alone never notices a Nix upgrade. That's why the cache helper also records which file the binary points to.
- Turbo's usual advice is to defer compinit, but that assumes nothing else calls compinit. Other tools' startup hooks can break that assumption, as mise's does here.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Your turn (optional, about 5–10 lines):** fill in `.zshrc-compdump-is-fresh` at `zshrc:166`. It decides when compinit can skip its checks (`-C`). The full checks cost about 15 ms, 9 ms of that in `compaudit`. Right now it always returns 1, which keeps the old behaviour. The two main options:
- **Rebuild once a day:** e.g. `[[ -n $1(#qN.mh-24) ]]`. It's simple, but a new completion (say from a brew install) can take up to a day to appear.
- **Rebuild only when completion files change:** return 1 if any folder in `$fpath` is newer than the dump (`[[ $dir -nt $1 ]]`). Adding or removing a file updates its folder's timestamp. This is precise and costs about a dozen timestamp checks. It misses a completion file edited in place, which is rare.

.zinit-self-update() {
    builtin emulate -LR zsh ${=${options[xtrace]:#off}:+-o xtrace}
    setopt extendedglob typesetsilent warncreateglobal

    if .zi-check-for-git-changes "$ZINIT[BIN_DIR]"; then
        [[ $1 = -q ]] && +zi-log "{pre}[self-update]{info} updating zinit repository{msg2}" \

        local nl=$'\n' escape=$'\x1b['
        local current_branch=$(command git -C $ZINIT[BIN_DIR] rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
        # local current_branch='main'
        local -a lines
        (
            builtin cd -q "$ZINIT[BIN_DIR]" \
            && +zi-log -n "{pre}[self-update]{info} fetching latest changes from {obj}$current_branch{info} branch$nl{rst}" \
            && command git fetch --quiet \
            && lines=( ${(f)"$(command git log --color --date=short --pretty=format:'%Cgreen%cd %h %Creset%s %Cred%d%Creset || %b' ..origin/HEAD)"} )
            if (( ${#lines} > 0 )); then
                # Remove the (origin/main ...) segments, to expect only tags to appear
                lines=( "${(S)lines[@]//\(([,[:blank:]]#(origin|HEAD|master|main)[^a-zA-Z]##(HEAD|origin|master|main)[,[:blank:]]#)#\)/}" )
                # Remove " ||" if it ends the line (i.e. no additional text from the body)
                lines=( "${lines[@]/ \|\|[[:blank:]]#(#e)/}" )
                # If there's no ref-name, 2 consecutive spaces occur - fix this
                lines=( "${lines[@]/(#b)[[:space:]]#\|\|[[:space:]]#(*)(#e)/|| ${match[1]}}" )
                lines=( "${lines[@]/(#b)$escape([0-9]##)m[[:space:]]##${escape}m/$escape${match[1]}m${escape}m}" )
                # Replace what follows "|| ..." with the same thing but with no
                # newlines, and also only first 10 words (the (w)-flag enables
                # word-indexing)
                lines=( "${lines[@]/(#b)[[:blank:]]#\|\|(*)(#e)/| ${${match[1]//$nl/ }[(w)1,(w)10]}}" )
                builtin print -rl -- "${lines[@]}" | .zinit-pager
                builtin print
            fi
            if [[ $1 != -q ]] {
                command git pull --no-stat --ff-only origin main
            } else {
                command git pull --no-stat --quiet --ff-only origin main
            }
        )
        if [[ $1 != -q ]] {
            +zi-log "{pre}[self-update]{info} compiling zinit via {obj}zcompile{rst}"
        }
        command rm -f $ZINIT[BIN_DIR]/*.zwc(DN)
        zcompile -U $ZINIT[BIN_DIR]/zinit.zsh
        zcompile -U $ZINIT[BIN_DIR]/zinit-{'side','install','autoload','additional'}.zsh
        zcompile -U $ZINIT[BIN_DIR]/share/git-process-output.zsh
        # Load for the current session
        [[ $1 != -q ]] && +zi-log "{pre}[self-update]{info} reloading zinit for the current session{rst}"

        # +zi-log "{pre}[self-update]{info} resetting zinit repository via{rst}: {cmd}${ICE[reset]:-git reset --hard HEAD}{rst}"
        source $ZINIT[BIN_DIR]/zinit.zsh
        zcompile -U $ZINIT[BIN_DIR]/zinit-{'side','install','autoload'}.zsh
        # Read and remember the new modification timestamps
        local file
        for file ( "" -side -install -autoload ) {
            .zinit-get-mtime-into "${ZINIT[BIN_DIR]}/zinit$file.zsh" "ZINIT[mtime$file]"
        }
    fi
} # ]]]

.zi-check-for-git-changes() {
    +zi-log "{dbg} checking $1"
    if command git --work-tree "$1" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree &> /dev/null; then
        if command git --work-tree "$1" rev-parse --abbrev-ref @'{u}' &> /dev/null; then
            local count="$(command git --work-tree "$1" rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...@'{u}' 2> /dev/null)"
            local down="$count[(w)2]"
            if [[ $down -gt 0 ]]; then
                return 0
            fi
        fi
        builtin print -P -- "Already up-to-date."
        return 1
    fi
} # ]]]

.zshrc-cache "$ZSHRC_CACHE/completions/_uvx" "${commands[uvx]}" uvx --generate-shell-completion zsh

# .zshrc-compdump-is-fresh <dump>
# Returns 0 when the completion dump can be trusted as-is, so compinit runs
# with -C: no compaudit and no rescan of fpath. Returns 1 to make compinit
# audit fpath and rebuild the dump if the set of completion files changed.
.zshrc-compdump-is-fresh() {
  local dump=$1
  # TODO(you): choose the invalidation policy. Returning 1 always keeps the
  # full check on every shell, which is the previous behavior.
  return 1
}

# compinit stays synchronous, not in Turbo: mise's hook (phase 9) runs its own
# `compinit -i` when compdef is missing and registers tool completions such as
# fnox. A later compinit from Turbo would run a second time and reset them.
() {
  local dump="${ZINIT[ZCOMPDUMP_PATH]:-${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zcompdump}"
  if .zshrc-compdump-is-fresh "$dump"; then
    ZINIT[COMPINIT_OPTS]=-C
  else
    ZINIT[COMPINIT_OPTS]=
  fi
  zicompinit
  # compinit sources the dump; zsh reads dump.zwc instead when it is newer.
  [[ -s $dump && ! "$dump.zwc" -nt $dump ]] && zcompile -- "$dump"
}
zinit cdreplay -q                          # compdef calls captured from plugins above

# Completions registered by code instead of fpath files. They need compdef.
# gcloud, gsutil and bq ship bash completions (loads bashcompinit).
[[ -r "${HOME}/Develop/google-cloud-sdk/completion.zsh.inc" ]] && \
  source "${HOME}/Develop/google-cloud-sdk/completion.zsh.inc"
compdef _gnu_generic zed

### 7. Turbo: loaded right after the first prompt ##############################
# Listed order is load order. fast-syntax-highlighting loads last because it
# wraps every ZLE widget that exists when it loads (fzf's included).
# blockf: git-ignore's completion is already linked into zinit's completions
# dir, so its fpath entry is not needed.
zinit wait lucid light-mode for \
    alexiszamanidis/zsh-git-fzf \
  blockf \
    laggardkernel/git-ignore \
    zdharma-continuum/fast-syntax-highlighting

### 8. Functions ##############################################################
# gitignore.io templates. Takes several names: `gi macos node`.
function gi() { curl -sLw "\n" "https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore/api/${(j:,:)@}" }

### 9. mise: must stay last ###################################################
# Its precmd hook rebuilds PATH from the snapshot taken at activation, which
# demotes every prepend after this line (e.g. nix bash below /bin/bash).
# Invoked by absolute path so it doesn't rely on PATH.
eval "$(~/.local/bin/mise activate zsh)"

import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("zshrc")
s = p.read_text()
a = s.index("# .zshrc-compdump-is-fresh <dump>")
b = s.index("zinit cdreplay -q")
s = s[:a] + '''# compinit trusts the dump for a day. For 24 hours after a full check it runs
# with -C: no compaudit and no rescan of fpath. After that, one shell runs
# the full check, which rebuilds the dump if completion files were added or
# removed, and touches it to start the next day. A completion installed
# today can take up to a day to appear. `rm ~/.zcompdump` picks it up now.
#
# compinit stays synchronous, not in Turbo: mise's hook (phase 8) runs its own
# `compinit -i` when compdef is missing and registers tool completions such as
# fnox. A later compinit from Turbo would run a second time and reset them.
() {
  setopt localoptions extendedglob
  local dump="${ZINIT[ZCOMPDUMP_PATH]:-${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zcompdump}"
  if [[ -n $dump(#qN.mh-24) ]]; then
    ZINIT[COMPINIT_OPTS]=-C
    zicompinit
  else
    ZINIT[COMPINIT_OPTS]=
    zicompinit
    # compinit rewrites the dump only when the file count changes.
    command touch -- "$dump"
  fi
  # compinit sources the dump; zsh reads dump.zwc instead when it is newer.
  [[ -s $dump && ! "$dump.zwc" -nt $dump ]] && zcompile -- "$dump"
}
''' + s[b:]
a = s.index("### 8. Functions")
b = s.index("### 9. mise")
s = s[:a] + s[b:]
s = s.replace("### 9. mise: must stay last ####", "### 8. mise: must stay last ####")
s = s.replace("#   8. Functions\n#   9. mise              Must stay last.", "#   8. mise              Must stay last.")
p.write_text(s)
PY

content.text:
I made all four changes. The shell now starts in about 70 ms, down from 83 ms before this round and about 196 ms originally.

**`zinit self-update` was wrong: zinit was not up to date.** It was 147 commits behind (Feb 2025 vs Sep 2026). The old version's update check has two bugs, both fixed upstream:
- It checked the git repo of the folder you ran it from, not zinit's own repo. Run from `~/Develop/dotfiles`, whose `main` has no remote to compare against, it just printed "Already up-to-date."
- It compared against the last-downloaded copy of upstream without downloading a fresh one first. So even run from the right place, it could miss new commits.

Since the old updater couldn't update itself, I did what it would have done by hand: a fast-forward pull to `c182cc5d` (26 Sep 2026) and a recompile of zinit's files. Running `zinit self-update` again now downloads first and correctly says "Already up to date." I re-ran the old-vs-new comparison on the new zinit, and key bindings, completions and command lookups all still match.

**The four annexes** add extra options you can put on a plugin line. Your config uses none of them, which is why I removed them:

| Annex | What it adds |
|---|---|
| `zinit-annex-as-monitor` | Watches a download page and installs new releases, for software not published on GitHub. |
| `zinit-annex-bin-gem-node` | Makes small launcher scripts for a plugin's programs instead of adding each plugin folder to PATH. It can also install Ruby gems, npm packages and pip packages inside a plugin's folder. |
| `zinit-annex-patch-dl` | Downloads extra files and applies patches to a plugin after it installs. |
| `zinit-annex-rust` | Installs a Rust toolchain and cargo packages inside a plugin's folder. |

Their folders are still on disk. Remove them with:
```
zinit delete zdharma-continuum/zinit-annex-{as-monitor,bin-gem-node,patch-dl,rust}
```

**Daily completion refresh** (`zshrc:162`):
- **Within 24 hours of the last full check:** compinit trusts the saved completion index (`compinit -C`) and skips its security audit and folder scan. I confirmed with a profiler that the audit no longer runs.
- **After 24 hours:** the next shell runs the full check, then updates the index file's timestamp. That touch is needed because compinit only rewrites the file when the number of completion files changes. Without it, the index would stay "old" and every shell after the first day would run the full check. I tested this with an old-dated index: it ran the full check and restarted the clock.
- **To see a new completion right away:** `rm ~/.zcompdump`. This is also noted in `README.md`.

**`gi` is removed.** The "Functions" section is gone, so mise is now phase 8. I updated the file header, the phase references and the README to match. `git ignore` still works: it resolves to git-ignore's command once the Turbo plugins have loaded.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The self-update bug came from `git --work-tree X`, which only sets which folder holds the files; git still finds the repository from the folder you're in. `git -C X` actually switches to X, which is the fix upstream made.
- A "rebuild daily" rule needs something to reset the clock. compinit leaves the index file untouched when nothing changed, so without the `touch` the 24-hour check would stay expired for good.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

None of this is committed yet (`zshrc`, `README.md`, `nix-migration.md`).

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jessearmand/.claude/skills/commit

# Commit Changes

Commit the change authorized by the user, preserving unrelated work and deriving
the message from the final staged diff. Honor an explicitly staged-only request;
otherwise use the task context to identify related tracked and new files.

## Scope and staging

- Inspect Git operation state, status, and staged and unstaged diffs. Do not create
  an ordinary commit during a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or revert, or with
  unmerged entries; use the operation-specific workflow when authorized.
- Include files and hunks that clearly belong to the requested change. Existing
  authorization covers related new files, including already-staged additions;
  do not ask for the same approval again. Ask when the intended scope is unclear.
- Leave unrelated unstaged and untracked files untouched without asking how to
  handle them. If unrelated content is already staged, resolve that scope conflict
  before committing; obtain authorization before changing the user's selection.
- Stage by explicit path, using partial staging for mixed-purpose files. Avoid
  broad commands such as `git add .`, `git add -A`, and `git commit -a`.
- Review the final staged diff for completeness, unrelated changes, secrets, and
  generated or machine-local state that does not belong in the repository.

## Validation

Use the repository's required checks and the relevant language guidance. Select
checks that exercise the changed behavior; a documentation-only commit does not
inherently require a full build or test suite.

Working-tree checks are sufficient when they exercise the same source and
configuration that will be committed. Reuse checks already run against that
state. If partial staging or excluded source/configuration could change the
result, validate the staged tree in isolation. Repository requirements or an
explicit request for exact-index validation also require isolation.

### Verify without unrelated untracked files

When isolation is needed, follow [staged-tree validation](references/staged-tree-validation.md).
This is also the exact-index procedure used by the `commit-staged` skill; retain
its staged-only scope when following that workflow.

Fix check failures within the authorized scope, review and stage the fixes, and
rerun affected checks. Ask before expanding the change. If required validation
fails or cannot run, report the failure or limitation and do not commit unless the
user explicitly authorizes proceeding. Never describe unrun checks as passing.

## Conventional Commit message rules

Use this format:

```text
<type>[optional scope][!]: <description>

[optional body]

[optional trailers]
```

Apply these rules:

- Use `feat` for a new user-visible capability and `fix` for a bug fix.
- Use `docs`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`, `perf`, `ci`, `build`, or `style` when one of those describes the change more accurately.
- Add a scope in parentheses only when it clarifies the affected subsystem, for example `fix(parser):`.
- Keep the description specific, imperative, and within 100 columns. Do not end it with a period.
- Add a body when the reason, behavior, tradeoff, or migration impact is not clear from the subject. Separate it with one blank line and wrap it within 120 columns.
- Explain why the change exists and what behavior changed; do not merely list filenames.
- Add trailer-style footers after another blank line, for example `Refs: #123`.
- Mark breaking changes with `!` before the colon or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

## Commit and report

- Reinspect the staged diff after validation. If the candidate changed, review it
  and rerun affected checks. Record the final index tree identifier before committing.
- Commit the index without bypassing hooks unless explicitly authorized. Do not
  amend, squash, push, or alter earlier commits without authorization.
- Compare `HEAD^{tree}` with the recorded candidate tree. If a hook or concurrent
  operation changed the committed content, report the discrepancy and inspect it;
  do not automatically amend or push.
- Report the commit identifier and subject, validation results and limitations,
  and any relevant work left outside the commit.

git add zshrc README.md nix-migration.md && git diff --cached --stat && TREE=$(git write-tree) && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
perf(zshrc): restructure into ordered phases and cut startup time by half

Split zshrc into numbered phases (instant prompt, helpers, environment, PATH, zinit,
completion, Turbo, mise) so load order and dependencies are explicit. Synchronous
startup drops from ~210 ms to ~95 ms; the first prompt appears ~120 ms earlier.

- Build PATH as one ordered list under `typeset -U path`, so precedence no longer
  depends on path_helper reordering and nested shells stop duplicating entries.
- Cache `brew shellenv`, `fzf --zsh` and the uv/uvx completion scripts in
  ~/.cache/zsh, regenerated when the producing binary changes or resolves to a new
  path (Nix store paths keep a fixed mtime).
- Put Homebrew site-functions on fpath before compinit, adding _brew and friends and
  replacing the manual _bun source.
- Keep compinit synchronous before mise, whose hook runs its own compinit and
  registers tool completions; trust the dump with -C for 24 hours between full checks.
- Load fast-syntax-highlighting in Turbo, last, so it also wraps fzf's widgets.
- Drop the unused zinit annexes, the no-op fzf-tab-completion plugin and the gi
  function (git-ignore covers it); load iTerm2 integration only inside iTerm2.

Update README and nix-migration.md to describe the new PATH and compinit ordering.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
